import math

# Data for 50 US states - unemployment insurance taxes in thousands of dollars
values = [735828, 536530, 417974, 350082, 271859, 257446, 235458, 222639, 209293, 190438,
          187735, 178509, 170442, 169376, 162666, 161146, 122270, 119199, 117667, 109606,
          101598, 100945, 97255, 71863, 66239, 65892, 64332, 64286, 62871, 61165,
          60537, 60206, 49175, 45885, 35205, 34037, 31420, 27166, 25975, 20345,
          19766, 18204, 17231, 15993, 13475, 12812, 12334, 10983, 8471, 7638]

# Sort in descending order
sorted_values = sorted(values, reverse=True)

print("Top 20 values (sorted descending):")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values[:20], 1):
    print(f"{i}: {v}")

# Hill estimator with k=7
k = 7

# Take top k+1 values for the Hill estimator
# x(1) >= x(2) >= ... >= x(n)
# The Hill estimator uses x(1) to x(k+1)
x_k_plus_1 = sorted_values[k]  # This is x(k+1) - the (k+1)th largest value

print(f"\nk = {k}")
print(f"x(k+1) = x({k+1}) = {x_k_plus_1}")

# Calculate the sum of log(x(i)/x(k+1)) for i=1 to k
log_sum = 0
for i in range(k):
    x_i = sorted_values[i]  # x(i) for i=0 to k-1 (which is x(1) to x(k))
    log_ratio = math.log(x_i / x_k_plus_1)
    log_sum += log_ratio
    print(f"i={i+1}: x({i+1}) = {x_i}, log({x_i}/{x_k_plus_1}) = log({x_i/x_k_plus_1:.4f}) = {log_ratio:.6f}")

print(f"\nSum of logs: {log_sum:.6f}")

# Hill estimator for tail index alpha
alpha = k / log_sum
print(f"\nHill tail index (alpha): {alpha:.6f}")

# Pareto tail exponent (xi) = 1/alpha
xi = 1 / alpha
print(f"Pareto tail exponent (xi = 1/alpha): {xi:.6f}")

# Alternative formula: xi = (1/k) * sum_{i=1}^k log(x(i)/x(k+1))
xi_alt = log_sum / k
print(f"\nAlternative calculation (xi = log_sum/k): {xi_alt:.6f}")

# Round to nearest thousandths
xi_rounded = round(xi, 3)
print(f"\nPareto tail exponent rounded to nearest thousandths: {xi_rounded}")

# Verify with the alternative formula
xi_alt_rounded = round(xi_alt, 3)
print(f"Alternative formula result: {xi_alt_rounded}")

- k is the number of upper order statistics used (tail cut)
- $X_{(k+1)}$ is the (k+1)th largest value

$$\hat{\alpha} = \frac{k}{\sum_{i=1}^{k} \log\left(\frac{X_{(i)}}{X_{(k+1)}}\right)}$$

and the Pareto tail exponent is:
$$\hat{\xi} = \frac{1}{\hat{\alpha}} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k} \log\left(\frac{X_{(i)}}{X_{(k+1)}}\right)}{k}$$
